title: U.S. House · California's 2nd District
area: Spans the North Coast of California from the Golden Gate Bridge north to the Oregon border, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Jared Huffman (D) placed first with 56.5% (139,662 votes) and Robin Littau (R) placed second with 11.4% (28,222 votes) out of 247,293 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Jared Huffman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 top-two primary outright with a majority of votes cast
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 2nd District (since 2013); Ranking Member, House Natural Resources Committee

summary.text: Jared Huffman is a Democratic attorney and environmental lawyer who served on the Marin Municipal Water District board and in the California State Assembly (2006-2012) before his 2012 election to Congress. Elected Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee in 2025, he is also a senior member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. His stated 2026 campaign priorities, per his Ballotpedia survey, are affordability, accountability and democracy.

background.text: Born February 18, 1964, in Independence, Missouri; graduated from William Chrisman High School in 1982.
Earned a bachelor's degree from UC Santa Barbara in 1986, where Wikipedia reports he was a three-time All-American volleyball player, and a law degree from Boston College Law School.

Worked as an attorney, including as associate attorney at McCutchen, Doyle, Brown & Enersen, managing partner at Boyd, Huffman & Williams, and managing partner at The Legal Solutions Group, LLP, and as a senior attorney for the Natural Resources Defense Council from 2001 to 2006.
Was elected to the Marin Municipal Water District board in 1994 and served 12 years, including three terms as board president.

Represented the 6th District in the California State Assembly from 2006 to 2012, where he chaired the Water, Parks & Wildlife Committee and the Assembly Environmental Caucus; he was barred from a fourth term by term limits.

Entered the 2012 race for California's 2nd District after 20-year incumbent Lynn Woolsey announced her retirement, won with more than 70% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and took office January 3, 2013; he has been re-elected since.

In 2025 House Democrats elected him Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, and he is a senior member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, per his Ballotpedia survey response.
Co-founded the Congressional Freethought Caucus with Rep. Jamie Raskin in 2018 and serves as its co-Chair; also a Vice-Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Lives in San Rafael with his wife, Susan, and their two children, according to Wikipedia.

priorities.text: Names affordability as a top priority, citing tariffs, trade wars and tax policy as drivers of rising costs for groceries, energy, healthcare and housing.
priorities.quote: Affordability - we have an affordability crisis in America, and Trump's tariffs, trade wars, actual wars, and massive tax giveaways to billionaires have caused everyday costs to skyrocket. We must put working families first and make lowering costs -- for groceries, energy and utility bills, healthcare, housing and more -- the top priority.

priorities.text: Says he will push for restored congressional oversight of the executive branch and a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, the President, and other executive branch officials.
priorities.quote: I will fight to hold Trump and others in the administration accountable by restoring serious oversight and investigations in a Democratic majority next Congress. I will also demand a total ban on stock trading (including prediction markets) by members of Congress along with the President and other executive branch officials.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, citing them as a cause of rising consumer costs.
positions.quote: Trump's tariffs, trade wars, actual wars, and massive tax giveaways to billionaires have caused everyday costs to skyrocket.

record.text: Elected by House Democrats as Ranking Member of the Committee on Natural Resources for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, including the Highways and Transit and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Robin Littau
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Board member, Enterprise Elementary School District (Redding, CA)

summary.text: Robin Littau is a Republican small-business owner and elected Enterprise Elementary School District board member in Redding who served in the U.S. Coast Guard from 1997 to 2001. According to her Ballotpedia survey response, she was born and raised in South Dakota and has lived in California for 28 years. She says her campaign centers on reducing taxation and burdensome legislation and on integrity, transparency and trust in government.

background.text: Says she was born and raised in South Dakota with farming and ranching roots; graduated from Sturgis Brown High School and attended Shasta College.
Served in the U.S. Coast Guard from 1997 to 2001 as a diesel mechanic (MK3), describing an honorable discharge and receiving a life-saving ribbon and a 9/11 ribbon.
Says she has lived in California for 28 years: Alameda (2 years), Bodega Bay (2 years), Sacramento (15 years) and Redding (10 years).
Owns and operates two sole-proprietor small businesses, Rockin Robin's Cleaning Service and Joyful Living Magazine.
Serves as an elected member of the Enterprise Elementary School District board (term 2024-2026), her only elected office listed on Ballotpedia.
Describes herself as a single mother of four children and says she has done community service including overseeing a neighborhood watch, a single mothers' support group and a weekly youth group.

priorities.text: Lists reducing taxation and burdensome legislation, restoring government integrity and transparency, and pursuing accountability for political waste and fraud as her main campaign messages.
priorities.quote: I want to create, replace, revise and approve common sense legislation that BENEFITS Americans and BUILDS America, by decreasing burdensome taxation and hindering legislation. Integrity filled leaders are essential for all leadership positions.

positions.summary: Campaign survey calls for decreasing taxation rather than raising it.

researchNotes: Robin Littau has no prior officeholder record beyond her local school board seat, so no additional record items beyond that background are documented. Biography gaps: Huffman's House 'About' page could not be retrieved, so his biography draws on Ballotpedia (including his own survey response) and Wikipedia; Littau's biography rests on her Ballotpedia survey response alone and has not been independently verified.
